Latin word

quīn

quīn (+ indicative)

interrogative adverb with the present indicative · Wiktionary

do …! why don’t you …? (urging); that … not (after a negative); why, indeed; nay even (adding something stronger: quīn etiam)

In this lexicon

  • do

    also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 1387: quid stās? quīn intrō īs?; Plaut. Asin. 597: quīn tū hīc manēs?

  • so … that

    also used · classical · Ter. Haut. 675: Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.

  • well …

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.26.3: quīn etiam noctibus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 405

  • Minimum āfuit quīn facerēs!: so close

    classical

  • quīn + subj.: without

    classical

Examples

  • Quid, taceam? quīn tū īs dormītum? — Dormiō, nē occlāmitēs.

    What, me be quiet? Why don’t you go to bed? — I am asleep: stop shouting.Plaut. Curc. 183–183b

    In the entry for do

  • quid stās? quīn intrō īs?

    Why are you standing there? Do go in.Plaut. Mil. 1387

    In the entry for do

  • Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.

    Nothing is so hard that it can’t be found out by searching.Ter. Haut. 675

    In the entry for so … that

  • Quīn hodiē!

    Why, this very day!Traupman 407

    In the entry for well …
